text: Henry Nolan’s motive to evoke nostalgia and a sense of belonging is directly linked to the thematic structure of his work through the use of the old mill as a central metaphor. By positioning the mill as a symbol of stability and resistance against modernity, Nolan structures the narrative to contrast the enduring value of tradition and community with the disruptive forces of change. This thematic framework serves his intent by grounding the reader in a specific, tangible setting that embodies the past, thereby reinforcing the emotional resonance of nostalgia and the comfort of communal identity in a rapidly evolving world.
